sentenceSets.sentence: The ambassador was known for being affable at receptions, putting even the most nervous guests at ease.

Sociable means enjoying company, close to affable, but doesn't necessarily convey the warmth and putting others at ease.
Gracious denotes courtesy and elegance, similar to affable, but emphasizes dignity over the friendliness and approachability that ease implies.
Charming denotes appeal, which would help guests feel at ease, but suggests a more calculated appeal than the genuine warmth of being affable.
Friendly is warm and approachable, very close to affable, but is more general and may lack the ease in conversation affable emphasizes.
Polite denotes courtesy, but is more formal and doesn't convey the warmth and approachability that putting nervous guests at ease requires.
Welcoming suggests open acceptance, fitting the comfort aspect, but doesn't emphasize the ease in conversation that affable denotes.
Genial means pleasant and kindly, very close to affable, but is slightly more formal in tone.
Aloof means distant and uninvolved; an affable person is approachable and warm—opposite temperaments.
Stern means severe; it would make nervous guests more uncomfortable, opposite to affable's effect.
Pompous means arrogant and self-important; an affable ambassador is humble and warm—opposite qualities.
